headline: Chinese tech companies have bought more than one million Nvidia gaming and workstation graphics chips to make up for a shortage of AI chips at home, the Financial Times reports.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the facts match the headline, but they rest on unnamed insiders in one report.
importance_line: It shows China still depends on US chips for AI even as its own output doubles, and, Tom's Hardware says, gamers and PC builders pay for it through scarce, expensive graphics cards; the figures come from unnamed industry insiders in one newspaper report and are not independently confirmed.
summary: The Financial Times reports, as relayed by Tom's Hardware, that Chinese tech companies bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation graphics chips, which comply with US export controls, to cover a shortfall of nearly 1.5 million AI chips, because Chinese factories are expected to make about 3.5 million against demand above 5 million. The report, which cites industry insiders, says the chips are weaker than Huawei's best but useful for simpler AI jobs, and Tom's Hardware adds that the buying is squeezing gaming cards, with the RTX 5090 now offered by only a handful of resellers at $7,199 or more against a $1,999 list price.
notes: Credit goes to the Financial Times as first reporter; the link is the Tom's Hardware page where the report was read, because the FT original is paywalled. The date of the FT report is not stated in the Tom's Hardware text.
